title: Post Grid Card
description: The post card the homepage "Tales from our trails" carousel renders, and the same card the LSX post-grid block uses wherever it appears. Landscape image above a tinted panel carrying a centred title, an italic byline in brand orange, and the excerpt. Measured from `.home #primary .home-post-carousel.lsx-block-post-carousel` on 2026-08-20: panel #F7F5F2 (neutral-200 exactly), title #60483B at 23px with sentence case, byline 13px italic #CC7F16, image 600x400 rendered at 204px tall. The byline is the only place on the site where brand orange carries running text; it is set on the tinted panel, where brand-500 measures 3.06:1 and cannot hold 13px copy, so it is carried at brand-600 here — the same AA correction style.md 12.5 applied to body copy and the pagination. The byline is a flex row of core/post-date and core/post-terms with a ". Posted in: " prefix and no block gap, which reproduces live's single line. Its prefix is held at regular weight with !important: assets/styles/core-post-terms.css bolds every `.wp-block-post-terms__prefix` at (0,1,0), a css-field rule compiles to `:root :where(…)` at the same specificity, and live's byline carries no bold at all. The last css rule hides the card's ruled tag footer on posts with no tags: `core/post-terms` returns an empty string when the taxonomy is empty (wp-includes/blocks/post-terms.php:57) but its wrapper group still renders, leaving a primary-300 rule dividing nothing. It is keyed off core's own `.wp-block-group` rather than a hand-rolled helper class, per AGENTS.md, so the pattern markup stays byte-identical to the signed-off dev composition and the dev front-page DB override needs no edit; it generalises correctly, since a post with no featured image empties the Media group and an empty box is no more wanted than an empty rule. `:not(:has(> *))` and not `:empty` — the groups keep the pattern's indentation, so they always hold whitespace text nodes and `:empty` never matches. Measured on the local homepage 2026-08-27: `:has()` and `:not()` both survive css-field sanitisation and compile to `:root :where(.wp-block-group.is-style-post-grid-card--N .wp-block-group:not(:has(> *)))`, so this stays JSON rather than dropping to enqueued CSS; `display` is set by nothing else on those groups, so zero specificity is enough and no !important is needed. The card's hover treatment is not here: a 4px rise and a step up the shadow scale (200 → 300) live in assets/styles/core-group.css, because the css field strips `:hover` outright and an `@media (prefers-reduced-motion)` block compiles its query text into the selector and then emits the inner rules at every setting. The resting shadow is an inline style written by the pattern's `style.shadow` attribute, so the hover value carries !important — no selector outranks an inline style, but an important author declaration does.

styles.css: & { overflow: hidden; height: 100%; } & .wp-block-post-terms__prefix { font-weight: var(--wp--custom--font-weight--regular) !important; } & .wp-block-group:not(:has(> *)) { display: none; }
